name: DOM Selector Finder
blurb: the shortest stable CSS selector for an element in pasted HTML
intro: Finds the element you name in pasted HTML and ranks the CSS selectors that pick it out alone: test ids first, then ids, names and semantic attributes, then classes. Generated ids and hashed class names (css-1x2y3, :r1:) are rejected, and a stable ancestor is used when the element has nothing of its own.

usage: Pass html (the markup containing the element), find (text, attr, selector or line), query (the text, name=value, selector or line number) and nth (1-based, when several match). It returns the best unique selector with a 0-100 stability score, every candidate with its match count and why it is or is not stable, the path to the element, and ready lines for querySelector, Playwright, Cypress, Selenium and Testing Library. Use it when writing end-to-end tests or scrapers; uniqueness is only against the pasted HTML.
